guide.title: Bleeding Control & Wound Care
guide.lead: Hands, then tourniquet or packing – fast. A tourniquet goes 5–7 cm above the wound and is tightened until the bleeding stops; packing goes deep into the wound with 3 minutes of hard pressure. Then clean and cover wounds, but don't close dirty ones.

steps.title: Place
steps.text: 5–7 cm (2–3 inches) above the wound, not over a joint; on the forearm or lower leg if there's room, otherwise above the elbow or knee.

steps.title: Tighten
steps.text: Until bleeding stops and the distal pulse disappears; lock the windlass.

steps.title: Not stopped?
steps.text: Tighten more, then a second tourniquet just above the first.

steps.title: Record
steps.text: Write the time on it. Never loosen it in the field – leave removal to the hospital.

steps.title: Pack
steps.text: Hemostatic or plain gauze pushed deep onto the bleeding point until the wound is full.

steps.title: Press
steps.text: Hard, for at least 3 minutes without peeking.

steps.title: Bandage
steps.text: Pressure dressing; reassess. Pelvic bleeding: binder at the greater trochanters.

sections.title: Wound care
rows: Irrigate thoroughly; don't close; record the animal and tetanus status; rabies per local guidance
Don't close with strips: infection risk
Stabilise in place; remove only if it blocks the airway or CPR
Wrap in moist sterile gauze, seal in a bag, place on ice – never directly on ice

quiz.q: Tourniquet applied but arterial bleeding continues. Next?
options: Tighten further until it stops; add a second above if needed
quiz.explanation: A loose tourniquet can increase venous bleeding.

quiz.q: Gunshot high in the groin: no room for a tourniquet. You:
options: Pack deep with hemostatic gauze and press hard for 3 minutes
Tourniquet as high as possible and hope

quiz.q: Below-knee amputation just under the knee with heavy bleeding. Tourniquet where?
options: On the thigh, 5–7 cm above the knee
quiz.explanation: No room below the knee; never over a joint.

quiz.q: A doctor on scene asks you to loosen a thigh tourniquet placed 20 minutes ago because bleeding has stopped. You:
options: Keep it on; removal is done in hospital with control ready

quiz.q: Can tourniquets work on the forearm?
options: Yes: place 5–7 cm above the wound if there's room
quiz.explanation: The old 'upper arm only' rule isn't supported.

quiz.q: Hemostatic packing needs pressure for at least:

options: Moist gauze, sealed bag, then on ice

quiz.q: Should a dog bite be closed with strips in the field?
Impaled knife in the thigh, bleeding controlled. You:
options: Stabilise it in place with bulky dressings
Cut it flush with the skin
quiz.explanation: Remove only if it blocks the airway or CPR.
Too high doesn't close the pelvis.

flashcards.question: First step for external bleeding
flashcards.answer: Firm direct pressure. If soaked, add layers or switch to a tourniquet (limb) or packing (junctional).

flashcards.question: Tourniquet rules
flashcards.answer: 5–7 cm above the wound, not over a joint, tighten until bleeding stops and the distal pulse is gone, record the time, never loosen in the field.

flashcards.question: Wound packing
flashcards.answer: Pack deep onto the bleeding point until full, press hard for at least 3 minutes, then a pressure dressing.

flashcards.question: Junctional bleeding
flashcards.answer: Groin, armpit or neck where a tourniquet won't fit: packing, pressure, rapid transport.

flashcards.question: Pelvic binder
flashcards.answer: Suspected pelvic fracture with shock: at the greater trochanters, not the iliac crests.

flashcards.question: Bite wounds
flashcards.answer: Irrigate thoroughly, control bleeding, dressing, don't close. Record animal details, rabies risk and tetanus status.

flashcards.question: Wounds not to close in the field
flashcards.answer: Deep, dirty, puncture, bite and crush wounds: closure traps bacteria.

flashcards.question: Amputated parts
flashcards.answer: Moist sterile gauze, sealed bag, on ice (not directly on ice); label and transport with the patient.

critical.scenario: Crash: a driver has bright red blood spurting from a deep forearm laceration, a large pool on the ground, pale and anxious.
critical.question: Sequence?

options.t: Direct pressure immediately, then a tourniquet 5–7 cm above the wound (forearm if room, otherwise upper arm), tighten until bleeding stops, record the time

critical.explanation: Then treat for shock and transport.

critical.scenario: Rebar through the inner thigh just below the groin crease; a thigh tourniquet hasn't stopped the steady bleeding.
critical.question: Next?

options.t: Leave the tourniquet, pack the wound around the bar with hemostatic gauze, press hard for 3 minutes, stabilise the bar, rapid transport

critical.explanation: Junctional wounds need packing and pressure.
critical.kpi: Manages junctional hemorrhage with an impaled object

critical.scenario: Stray-dog bite: deep punctures on the palm, minor bleeding, dog gone. Tetanus status unknown.
critical.question: Management?

options.t: Irrigate well, control bleeding, dressing, don't close; record the dog's details and that it can't be observed; hospital for rabies and tetanus assessment

critical.kpi: Provides appropriate bite wound care and documentation
